chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Ali ibn Asbat from Ibn Riab from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

I said to him, 'A man gave his wife the option of divorce.' He said, 'The option belongs to her as long as they remain in their session; when they separate, there is no option for either of them.' I said, 'May God perfect you, but if she divorces herself three times before they separate from their session,' he said, 'It will not be more than one [divorce], and he has more right to take her back before her waiting period is completed.' And indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) gave his wives the option, and they chose him, so that became a divorce. I said to him, 'If they had chosen themselves, it would have been for us.' He said to me, 'What do you think of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) if they had chosen themselves? Would he have kept them?' The approach in these narrations, despite the difference in their wording and the contradiction in their meanings, is to carry them upon a type of taqiyyah (dissimulation), because they are consistent with the belief of the general public. And if we did not carry these narrations upon what we said, we would have to discard the narrations that contained that this was not a real event, and that this was something specific to the Prophet (peace be upon him), and that this was something that my father narrated from Aisha, and whatever words followed that pattern, and we were unable to act upon them in any manner, and that is not permissible in any case.

key_terms.العَامَّة: The general public or Sunni Muslims, often contrasted with the Shia in theological discussions.
key_terms.تَخْيِير: The act of giving someone the choice or option, specifically in the context of divorce.
key_terms.تَقِيَّة: Dissimulation or precautionary concealment of one's true beliefs, often used in Shia theology to explain apparent contradictions in narrations.
key_terms.رَجْعَة: The husband's right to take back his wife during the waiting period (iddah) after a revocable divorce.
key_terms.عِدَّة: The waiting period a woman must observe after divorce or death of her husband before she can remarry.
key_terms.مَجْلِسُهُمَا: The session or gathering where the divorce option is exercised; its duration affects the legal validity.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a husband gives his wife the option of divorce and she chooses it immediately?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies that 'takhyyir' (divorce option) is a unilateral right of the wife during the marital session, where a pre-separation choice results in a single irrevocable divorce (talaq mughallazah) while the husband retains the right of return (ruju'). The scholar highlights a key Shia interpretive nuance: the Prophet’s choice of his wives is viewed through taqiyyah to align with Sunni jurisprudence, thereby preserving contradictory reports without discarding them as specific to the Prophet alone.
